verdict.rationale: Rainforest can be driven headlessly through its own server-side API. Long-lived API keys authorize servers to call the API, payins and merchant onboarding can be done via the API instead of the embedded UI components, an OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec is published, and a sandbox environment with test cards supports end-to-end testing. However, nothing documents CI-specific usage, such as a CLI, CI pipeline guidance or automated test-run tooling. missing for 10: an official CLI or CI integration guide, documented CI/test-automation workflows, independent hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: An API key is a long-lived credential that authorizes servers to communicate with the Rainforest API.
Platforms that are approved by Rainforest can send sensitive merchant onboarding data, including bank accounts and Social Security Numbers, to Rainforest via a direct to API integration.
Detailed guides and walkthroughs, full end-to-end sandbox testing, realtime API logs, and more.
Rainforest supports OpenAPI Specifications (OAS) of the Rainforest API, version 3.1.0.
